font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: normal;\"\u003EPreload :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: normal;\"\u003EPreload is volume of blood received by the heart. Basically preload is stretch.It is the ventricular stretch at the end of diastole. Occurrence : during diastole Depends on : The amount of ventricular filling. Preload is a volume. Affecting factors : venous blood pressure and the rate of\u0026nbsp; venous return.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: normal;\"\u003EAfterload :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: normal;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Afterload is the pressure that the Chambers of the heart must generate in order to eject blood out of heart. Occurrence : during systole Depends on :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"color: rgb(117, 117, 117); font-size: 15px; letter-spacing: normal;\"\u003EThe arterial blood pressure and vascular tone. Afterload is a pressure. Here we discuss our individual patient’s problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient’s clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This E log book also reflects my patient-centered online portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comment box.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDecember 05,2023\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EI have been given this case to solve in an attempt to understand the topic of \" patient clinical data analysis\" to develop my competency in reading and comprehending clinical data including history, clinical findings investigations and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 60 year old female resident of suryapet farmer by occupation came to the OPD with\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECHIEF COMPLAINTS :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESwelling of both legs since 20 days\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBreathlessness since 3 days\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently asymptomatic 3 years ago when she developed lower back pain which was sudden in onset gradually progressive no aggravating and relieving factors and she noticed decreased urine output that is not associated with frequency, urgency, burning micturition\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThere is bilateral pedal edema which was insidious in onset gradually progressive intially extending upto ankle then progressed to knee which was of grade 3\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe has shortness of breath which was sudden in onset gradually progressive grade 3 aggravated on walking relevied by taking rest\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThen she was taken to hospital where they diagnosed as kidney failure and was on medication for 6 months then started on dialysis twice a week\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"letter-spacing: 0.2px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp; 2 days backshe was brought to the hospital due to severe shortness of breath grade 4 aggravated on lying down position and slightly relieved on sitting\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPresently Pedal edema in both legs extending upto the knee. She was having tremors of both hands and legs which are occurring infrequently\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ehistory of orthopnea present\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of evening rise of temperature\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of abdominal pain\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPAST HISTORY : known case of hypertension since 1year\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of diabetes asthma epilepsy tuberculosis\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETREATMENT HISTORY : On regular dialysis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe is on medication nifedipine and furosemide\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;PERSONAL HISTORY : Before illness : mixed diet, normal appetite, adequate sleep, regular bowel and bladder moments no addictions and allergies\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfter illness : Diet : consuming foods like idly milk in small quantities reduced appetite, reduced bowel and bladder\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDAILY ROUTINE : BEFORE ILLNESS :\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ewakes up at 6 am does house hold work like cooking, washing utensils till 8:30am then she eats rice with pickle or curry as breakfast and then goes to field. Eats lunch at 1:00 pm and then comes back home at5:00 pm does house hold work and drinks a cup of tea. Dinner at 8:30 pm and goes back to sleep at 10:00pm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAFTER ILLNESS: stopped working 2 years back from then she just stays at home\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFAMILY HISTORY : not significant\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneral examination : patient was conscious coherent cooperative thin built moderately nourished\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPallor present. Bilateral pedal edema present. No cyanosis clubbing lymphadenopathy\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVitals : pulse rate : 104 bpm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERespiratory rate : 32 cpm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETemperature : a febrile\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESpo2 : 84%\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBlood pressure : 100\/80 mm hg\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
